name: Taxon co-occurrence
description: Which taxa are found together and which exclude each other. For the most prevalent taxa of a long profile table, every pair is scored on presence across samples: phi coefficient, lift and Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg control. The heatmap clusters taxa by their co-occurrence so groups that travel together become visible.

inputs.label: Taxon profiles (long)
inputs.description: One row per taxon per sample with read counts. A group role allows restricting the analysis to one group.

top_n.title: Taxa to compare
top_n.description: The most prevalent taxa that enter the pairwise comparison.

min_prevalence_pct.title: Minimum prevalence (%)
min_prevalence_pct.description: Taxa present in fewer samples are left out.

group.title: Restrict to group
group.description: A value of the group role; empty uses every sample.

q_threshold.title: Significance (q)
q_threshold.description: Pairs with a Benjamini-Hochberg q below this are flagged.

rank.title: Taxonomic rank
rank.description: When the table maps a rank role, use taxa of this rank only.

min_reads.title: Minimum reads per sample
min_reads.description: Samples with fewer retained reads are dropped; 0 keeps every sample.

remove_artifacts.title: Remove curated artifacts
remove_artifacts.description: Drop taxa on curation lists with the artifact role first.

outputs.name: cooccurrence_pairs
outputs.description: One row per taxon pair: counts of the four presence combinations, phi, lift, Fisher p, q, relation and curated roles.

outputs.name: cooccurrence_heatmap
outputs.description: Phi between every pair of the compared taxa, taxa ordered by clustering.

outputs.name: strongest_pairs
outputs.description: The pairs with the smallest q as bars of phi: blue co-occur, red exclude.

citation: Built with pandas, NumPy, SciPy (Virtanen et al. 2020) and Plotly. Phi coefficient (Yule 1912), Fisher's exact test (Fisher 1922), Benjamini-Hochberg (1995); average-linkage clustering of 1 - phi. See README.md.
